# kb

> kb is a memory plugin for Claude Code. It keeps what the agent learns as plain markdown notes in a local git repo. Every new session gets a small index of the notes, and a note loads only when it applies: when the agent runs a command, hits an error, or reads a file that the note names. kb is free and open source (MIT), and it is pre-release.

kb is for people who use Claude Code. It fills the gap between the two places for memory that Claude Code already has:

- CLAUDE.md holds the rules that you state. Every session loads all of it.
- Auto memory holds what Claude Code saves by itself. It loads all of it at every start.
- kb keeps what the agent learns. A fixed character budget (8,000 characters by default) caps what a session start loads, however large the store grows.

## Install

Requirements: Claude Code 2.1.275 or later, Bun 1.x and git, on macOS or Linux. Windows is not supported.

1. In Claude Code, run `/plugin install kb --marketplace jrnxf/plugins`.
2. In `~/.claude/settings.json`, set `"autoMemoryEnabled": false` and allow `Bash(kb help)`, `Bash(kb show *)`, `Bash(kb search *)` and `Bash(kb add *)`.

## Commands

- `/kb:save` saves what the session learned. `/kb:clear` saves, then clears the session only if the save worked.
- `/kb:recover` saves a session that ended with no save, up to 7 days later.
- `/kb:audit` reviews stale notes. You keep, rewrite, merge, promote or trash each one.
- `kb serve` opens the store as a page in your browser on this machine.
